utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I see the witness is not here. I believe somebody has got housekeeping. Is that the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. My goal is to make it to the -- November 20th without raising a housekeeping matter. So I'm still on track. I think it's Mr. Milovancevic who wants to raise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. We have a housekeeping matter. According to the schedule of witnesses, after General Djukic, whose examination is under way the Witness MM-114, Dragan Knezevic, was supposed to appear. We have obtained safe conduct for him for the Trial Chamber. As he's a refugee we have obtained temporary travelling document for him and delivered to him the Court's guarantees but he lost all these documents so that he's unable to appear on Monday. So instead of the witness Knezevic, on Monday, Mile Dakic should appear, who was otherwise scheduled to appear after Knezevic and then the normal schedule would be followed, MM-106 Zoran Lakic and 092, Nada Pupovac. I'm raising this matter and addressing a request to the Trial Chamber and to the learned colleagues from the OTP to appreciate the situation. We have taken steps for new travelling documents to be issued to this witness which is not all that simple because he's a refugee and can be issued such documents only for seven days. So that he will appear somewhat later and as we will have the witness Mile Dakic on Monday, can I ask the Trial Chamber to rule on our submission in accordance with Rule 92(F) and this is the only matter which I wish to raise at this point. Sorry, 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The only problem -- not problem -- the only point that I hear from what you're saying is that you're putting 106 before 92, but according to the order that we have, 92 comes before 106. So that after -- if 84 comes next week, then it's going to be followed by 114, then 92 had to come in before 106. Are you wanting to change that as well, to swap 106 with 92?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I was confused with the numbers and with the sequence of the witnesses. The only thing that we wished to do was to inform the Court that the next witness will not be the witness Knezevic, MM-114, but before him as the first witness following this one, will be MM-084, Mile Dakic, and a ruling according to 92 ter is requested, and I just mentioned the other witnesses according to this -- it's not the actual sequence of their appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, you know, I'm not sure -- I'm a little surprised that we are being told about this now, that is the point of view of the Prosecution. I'm not sure why we didn't -- weren't informed about this sooner because, of course, now we are being -- we will have to cross-examine this witness on Monday and we have not expected to reach this witness until later in the week. And we have to completely shift gears now. But I think, you know, we'll do it and I just wish -- I just would ask that a little more effort be made to inform us about things, maybe they just found out a few minutes ago. I would be surprised but, yeah, so we'll cross-examine on Monday, that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm not quite sure what ruling the Defence is asking for. 92 ter, what specific ruling do you want under Rule 92 ter, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, under 92 ter, a written statement of a witness is introduced and he's orally examined in part. In order for the written statement to be introduced, a ruling by the Trial Chamber is required and that is what I had in mind and also, I do not expect that the examination of the witness Dakic, the cross-examination, that is, will begin on Monday. I do not think that that is realistically feasible. In my view, you cannot start before Tuesday and even later than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which statement do you want admitted in terms of 92 ter, of Dakic or of somebody else? Of Dakic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dakic's, Your Honours, yes. MM-084, the witness Mile Dakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, Your Honour, this is probably my fault but now I'm confused. After this witness, Mr. Djukic, 114 will not appear so then who is the next witness going to be? I'm lost now 84? So dropping out is 92 and 106.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. They're not dropping out, they're just shifting a step below.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then I'm further confused by what Defence counsel says, we won't start the cross-examination on Monday, because if he's 92 ter I thought that he would put his statement in and we start cross-examination. So I'm a little confused then and I would appreciate guidance so that we can prepare. Tuesday, of course, we have no court, I believe. I believe that's the holiday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, Tuesday we have a holiday. I don't know why he says so but any clarification I can give you is that we've got Djukic on the box now. According to the request by the Defence, the next witness is 84 and then the -- the witnesses follow as they stand. 84 followed by 114 followed by 92 followed by 106 and he's now asking that the 92 ter statement of 84 be admitted into evidence now so that it be handed in by his calculation you will not have reached 84 by Tuesday or my Monday. I don't know what he bases that on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would certainly appreciate some clarification on that because we believe that this witness will be done by this week so we will at least start with Mile Dakic on Monday so I would be grateful to know why it is we won't reach cross-examination. Then with respect to the 92 ter motion, we do not oppose his evidence coming in via 92 ter. Of course, it cannot be admitted now. He has to come to court and swear to it, and then it's admitted, but we don't oppose that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This whole discussion is taking a little longer than I thought it was going to take. I said yesterday that these things must be dealt with by way of written motions. I was trying to make this exception because Mr. Milovancevic stood up on this point. Can you deal with this by way of written motions? Ask what you want to ask for, Mr. Milovancevic. Let the Prosecution respond, then you get a written decision. May we call the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me remind you that you made a declaration yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just remind you that you are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth today. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Djukic.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: We shall continue with the examination-in-chief which started yesterday. Tell me, Mr. Djukic, do you remember what was the decisive factor or do you remember when the incidents directed against the Yugoslav People's Army started along all directions including the area in which you were and what particular point in time or do you associate the beginning of such incidents with?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incidents directed against the Yugoslav People's Army started after the meeting of the president of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Franjo Tudjman, with the political leadership of the Croatian Democratic Union in the region of Dalmatia, in the place called Trogir, which meeting was held sometime in early May. I believe on the 5th of May 1991. From that time on, ensued operations or rather actions of cutting down electricity supplies, telephone lines, intercepting individual military vehicles, searching military personnel, seizing weaponry, and all other such incidents targeting members of the Yugoslav People's Army. In parallel with that were also organised actions against the local Serb population precisely in the zone of responsibility of the Knin Corps. I can adduce only several such incidents, namely the situation in Zadar proper, something which happened somewhat earlier, in fact, a couple of days, two or three days earlier, when in just one evening after Franko Lisica, a Croatian policeman was killed and buried, about 30.000 residents of Zadar assembled and in the evening demolished according to the police department of Zadar's report, about 123 shops and buildings belonging to Serbs, which was to be followed by demolition on a wider area so that we had figures and data officially confirmed by the official organs of Croatia, namely the total figure was about a thousand facilities in that area that were demolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: At that time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Sorry, sorry, the interpreter did not hear the question, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just hold on. The interpreter did not hear your question, Mr. Perovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you can please make a pause so that you don't overlap. Can you ask the question again, please, Mr. Perovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: My question was: What was the situation with the Croatian officers, members of the 9th Corps at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of the Croatian officers, who were in the 9th corps, had their apartments, resided in cities on the littoral Zadar, Sibenik and Split, most of them in Split. And over the weekends, they were able to go and see their families or, according to the regulations then in force, they could get leave every seven days and they had to pass through those areas. They would be stopped by the police, they would be searched, their arms seized, they would be apprehended and detained which was totally illegal at that time for members of the Yugoslav People's Army to be treated in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the culmination of incidents of this kind, i.e., attacks on members and facilities of the Yugoslav People's Army? Can you associate that with a particular point in time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wholesale attack on all the units, and facilities, i.e., barracks and depots of the Yugoslav People's Army, was publicly declared and ordered by the president of the Republic of Croatia on the 15th of September 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Perovic, before you go on, page 7, lines 10 to 19, I'm not understanding. It says the majority of Croatian officers who were in the 9th Corps had their apartments and resided in the cities and they were stopped by the police over the weekend they would go to see their families. They would be stopped by the police and searched and their arms seized. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall answer that through the witness and clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Is this about, Mr. Djukic, officers of the Yugoslav People's Army of Croatian ethnicity who had flats in Zadar, Sibenik and other towns that you enumerated?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those officers who were in serving in the 9th Corps in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Is this sufficient, Your Honours, as an answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: I wanted to double check that that was correct. Thank you. I'll comprehend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll tell you what I don't understand in that sentence. What I don't understand is the statement "resided in." Let's go back to that page. "The majority of the Croatian officers who were in the 9th Corps had their apartments, resided in cities." I'm not quite sure what that means, on the literal Zadar Sibenik and Split, most of them in Split. Who resided in these apartments? They were resided in by who, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it would be best for the witness to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: These are JNA officers who are of Croat ethnicity serving in the 9th Corps, which is headquartered at Knin. Could you please explain whether these officers had their apartments in other cities?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. They had their apartments in the towns that I enumerated. Their families lived there but they served in Knin. They served in the headquarters of the 9th Corps. I can explain on my own example. I served in Knin but my apartment was in Herceg Novi in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So these people had their apartments in cities on -- like Zadar, Sibenik, and Split? That's what it means. Thank you very much, Mr. Perovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, on the 15th of September 1991, as you stated, ordered by the president of Croatia, Franjo Tudjman, there is a general blockade of the barracks and facilities of the JNA throughout the Croatian territory, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What is happening within the area of responsibility of the 9th Corps after that order issued by President of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that order was issued, what happened was that Zitnic depot, which is a munitions and mines and explosives depot located near to Drnis along the Drnis-Sibenik road, they blockaded, "they" meaning the paramilitary forces of Croatia, a depot and the base of the 55th navy rocket base Trbovnje, and both barracks and all other facilities in the garrison of Sinj were blockaded as well and that garrison was part of the 9th Corps because 316th Brigade was, by formation, part of the 9th Corps of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: We will come back to those events later on. Now I'd like to broach another subject. Mr. Djukic, do you know what happened to the weapons of the Territorial Defence of the Knin municipality? Where was it and who had control over it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Complete weapons of the Territorial Defence of Knin was located at a depot entitled Krka, close to Knin itself. There was a fortified facility housing the weapons and materiel of the Territorial Defence of. That depot was guarded by sentries of the JNA and those who may enter the depot had to contact the guards commander to perform their tasks at that depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: So this was a JNA depot?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a depot of the Territorial Defence of which was part of a depot of the JNA because there were several facilities there. One of them was designated for Territorial Defence of. Other buildings were depots of weapons, materiel, of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What do you know about the decision of the SFRY decision dated 9th of January 1991? What kind of a decision it was?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SFRY Presidency took a decision on the 9th of January on the disarming of all parapolice and paramilitary forces in the territory of the SFRY which concerned mainly the disarming of parapolice and paramilitary forces in the territory of Croatia and Slovenia, and in certain areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Is it known to you whether Croatia at that time observed that Presidency of SFRY decision?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to explain just one thing. On the basis of that order, each subordinated command and the command of the 9th Knin Corps, established a commission tasked with accepting in receipt of these units' arms and to warehouse them at JNA depots. Within my area of responsibility where I was commander, we nominated two officers, Slavulj Dusan, and another officer, a non-commissioned officer, Petko Milan, to head this commission. It was in -- the commission worked in the north of Knin and it was tasked to take video footage and prepare documentation for the receipt from citizens and all those bearing arms of the weapons. They had to be brought to the northern barracks in Knin. It is known to me that the Knin police station or the MUP of Knin handed over 100 automatic rifles and three heavy -- and heavy guns, machine-guns, from the territory of the municipality of Knin. I know that another commission was organised in the garrison of Benkovac but I don't know the details about the weapons so handed in. It is known to me that in the territory of overall Croatia, a total of 150 rifles were handed over and we have data of that in the General Staff of the JNA. At that time, Croatia had imported 30.000 automatic rifles from abroad, mainly from Hungary. It handed over 150, not of these but some old trophy weapons, just to take a red herring across the path.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djukic, do you know what Vance Plan is and when was it presented to the public?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- I am quite familiar with it because we had to familiarise ourselves with it and implement it. It is the international community's Security Council of the UN document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: When was it published?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared, as far as I know, in December 1991, and its implementation started, as far as I know, in January 1992, but some elements of that plan commenced in December 1991 with the deployment of monitors between two sides in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did this -- did this plan envisage for the Republic of Serbian Krajina to have its own military and police?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says literally in the plan that the Republic of Serbian Krajina may hold its own police and military. When it comes to the military, what is mentioned there is Territorial Defence, which ought to have been demobilised, heavy weaponry had to be depoted with a double key system, under double lock and key, which was observed in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. The JNA had to withdraw, pursuant to that agreement, by the 19th or 20th May of that same year, 1992. And as far as the police is concerned, it is expressly stated there that the Republic of Serbian Krajina could have its own police and that the police would encompass regular police, just as any country in the world, and regular police [as interpreted]. So they -- they could form regional police and the government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina adopted decision to that effect and they implemented it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was demobilisation of Territorial Defence units in the RSK done in time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the report submitted to the Security Council of the UN, submitted in August 1992, by peacekeepers within the RSK, it is stated there that the JNA withdrew by that time, when the report was drafted, from the territory of the RSK, that the Territorial Defence was demobilised and the weapons were depoted pursuant to the Vance Plan, in the manner envisaged by the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could I get clarity? Maybe it's better to get it now than later. On page 12, at line 19, the witness says, let me start at line 17 where the sentence begins, "And as far as the police concerned it is expressly stated that the Republic of Serbian Krajina could have its own police and that the police would encompass regular police, just as any other country in the world, and regular police." Regular police and regular police. Are there two different types of regular police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a mistake. There is just one type of regular, ordinary police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that it is a mistranslation -- misinterpretation. The witness mentioned regular and regional police, as two different police forces or forms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the witness once more because I had exactly the same question so the police encompassed what? Something which is usual in the rest of the world and something different. Could you repeat what you wanted to say? Because we have a problem with the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to the Vance Plan, it was envisaged for a regular police force to exist, and regional police units were also envisaged. So ordinary or regular police, which functions, and a part of police that they called regional police, in that document. Police which may -- formed in regions. May I explain this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, witness. I would like an explanation because in my mind, I can envisage regular police being regionalised so I don't understand the difference between regular and regional. So I still want to get an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that through the subsequent two or three questions, I will have clarified this dilemma and I would like to ask a couple of questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Perovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, when you say regional police or regional police forces, what do you mean by that? What kind of police forces do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police forces that, in the Republic of Serbian Krajina, were dubbed "special units of police."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what we are going to discuss right now. When were these special units of police formed or established?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were established on the 28th of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: When was the -- then was the date of the establishment of the administration of special units of police within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know under whose orders?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That administration of special units of police was established, sir, under the orders of the General Staff of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: I would like to have the Prosecutor's 65 ter document 1334 to be brought on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that, you are saying that the date of the establishment of administration of special units of police within the Ministry of the Interior, which Ministry of the Interior of the SAO Krajina or of the federal -- Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Would you like to explain that, Mr. Djukic? Which Ministry of the SFRY or of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was not issued by a ministry of the SFRY but the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: But that administration?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had two lines of responsibility. The head of that administration was directly responsible to the Minister of the Defence, to Stojan Spanovic, the then minister, and the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to come to that.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other line of responsibility went to the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, I'm going to ask you about that later. Now we have the -- on the screens the document that I sought. Can we go to page 2 of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. -- I'm sorry, have I, has my question been answered? I want to know when the witness said that the date of the establishment of the administration of special units of police within the Ministry of the Interior, I just want to know which Interior, which Ministry of the Interior, is it the Ministry of the Interior of the SAO Krajina or is the Ministry of the Interior of the SFRY? He has just told us that the instruction didn't come from the Ministry of the Interior of the SFRY. I understand that. I understand that he says the orders came from the General Staff of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm reading what's written here, General Staff of the JNA. Now, all I want to know is this Ministry of the Interior within which the special units of police were established, it is the Ministry of the Interior of which government? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document resolves this matter, and over the next two questions, I will have demonstrated that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before he sees the document, surely this is his testimony. He must know which Ministry of the Interior he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: When you're talking about the Ministry of the Interior, which ministry do you mean, Mr. Djukic, of Yugoslavia or of SAO Krajina or --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Interpretation] -- at this moment in my headphones. Shall I try to continue and see whether it's been sorted out?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, would you read the heading and the title of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Order strictly confidential number 1943-1 of the Federal Secretary for National Defence of the 28th of April 1992, organisational and establishment changes."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- I am familiar with it. I've received excerpts from this order, from subordinated organs, and I am familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please be so kind as to read out for us the text on the first page, which is in capitals, and it starts with the word "I order". Just the capitals.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First under one it says, "Organisational changes."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: So "I order" and then?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First it says, "Organisational changes," and then it goes on to say, "in the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now turn to page 3 of the original version? That is actually page 2 in the English translation. In the B/C/S it is the third page. Can we see that on the monitor? In the English translation it is the second page. B/C/S, page 3. 1676 is the mark on the page. Yes. It is the third page and in the English translation it is page number 2. May I just -- so it is item 10 of this document that I'm interested in. Now we have item 11, point 11. So it will be at the bottom of the second page, also in the B/C/S version, probably. So item 10, please. That's it. Yes. At the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Item 10. Will you please read item 10 of this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 10, "To set up in peace a department of the special units of the militia or police of the Republic of Serbian Krajina according to a list of duties to be filled with active military personnel, number 270.308. The administration shall be subordinated to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So is this an order whereunder was established the administration of the special units of the police of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Once again, who formed that administration?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, and according to the facts, this administration was formed by the army, namely the Federal Secretary for National Defence, i.e. the federal Ministry for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask Your Honours to have this document tendered as evidence of the Defence, tendered into the file, case file?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Well, actually I have a problem because it is not completely translated. There is only an excerpt in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite correct, Your Honours. We ourselves have observed that the Prosecution has unfortunately failed to translate this document in its entirely but we shall do so. You can see when we turn to page 4 of the original version, which I was just about to show to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection to it going in, and it being translated completely. I'm not sure we failed but I'll let that one slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say, "and it being translated completely," translated by who? We've got to know who is bearing the responsibility to do that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, as it's the Defence's proposed exhibit and offered to do it I'm happy to defer to them. If they have a problem getting it translated, they should get in touch with us and we can assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that okay, Mr. Perovic? You'll attend to the translation and if you have difficulties, you can ask your colleagues to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my colleague, the Prosecutor, and the Trial Chamber. There is no problem. We shall be submitting subsequently the untranslated part as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. As it is not such a large document I was thinking that would be feasible, in fact. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. The document as appears on the screen is admitted into evidence as a Defence Exhibit under -- on the condition that it will be translated in full and filed. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number 978.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Perovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: While we still have this document on the screen, I should like to use that, and can we have the page 4 of the original version, 1676 is the page number, point 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, it is the third page of the original version, point 11. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's the third page and at the same time, it's page number 4 in the electronic document because the cover note was the page 1, speaking of the B/C/S original, yes? So it's page 3 which is the first page, the fourth page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: So item 11 is what we are interested in, Mr. Djukic. Would you please comment on what I'm going to read out for you? Item 11 reads, "Attached to the ministry, within the Ministry of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, in peacetime and in war, police brigades should be set up according to the following." And then there is a whole series listed. And then it goes on to say, at the end of item 11, "Brigades shall in peace and in war be subordinated to the administration of the special units of the police of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." You have understood what I've read out to you?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Was this order complied with?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us more specifically what was done to implement this order?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this order, there were formed first of all the administration of the special police units on the heading which was I myself, and we also started with the setting up of the brigades of the special police units sometime in May, but up until they were disbanded they were never actually brought to full complement because this hinged upon numerous circumstances, both on the ground and in respect of the capacity to replenish these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have at least I have a problem because my document in English ends at page 2, so this item 11 you are referring to, I don't have, and I'm not sure -- I don't know what you're talking about. We are out of court -- you are the only people in court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the part which was not, has not been translated, Your Honour. That is page 4 of the original B/C/S version. Item 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But at least we would have expected the part that you're going to use in court you have translated. Now, I can tell you, we only have this item 10 that you referred to, then below that is item Roman 3, I issue the order for organisation. And then A, merging, open bracket peace, closed bracket of the brigades of the police are number T, that's all. That's all we have so we don't follow what you and the witness are talking about which relates to item 11 as you referred to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that this is perhaps a problem, Your Honours, and I shall therefore rephrase my question in order to avoid having to invoke point 11, if you're agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. I don't want you to -- not to refer to point 11, Mr. Perovic. I would like you to refer to point 11. In fact you have already referred to it and you have got a couple of answers on questions about it, but all I'm just saying is we are in the difficulty that we don't know what you're talking about because we don't have the document before us, and I would have imagined that that portion of that document which you intended to use you would have translated for us, if you didn't see it necessary to translate the entire document, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: In addition, this number 11 is not really legible in the original, in the first line, one word, at least for someone who doesn't speak the language, is not being readable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that, this remark of Your Honours, and I actually withdraw this question related to item 11. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that, Mr. Perovic. If you can make sure that as soon as possible after this we get the translation of item 11, even before you give us a translation of the whole document, at least then we can correlate it with what you have said with the witness. I don't want you to withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And I have another confusion also. Actually that started with our debate but which Ministry of the Interior, you remember, on page 14 and 15, and Mr. Perovic, I think, in fact, you used in your question the word Ministry of the Interior, and then the whole debate came up, which Ministry of the Interior. Now we hear from the document and from the translation it is the Ministry of Defence, and in this number 11, it just says "Pri ministarstvu Republika Srpska Krajina [B/C/S spoken]," and so on so no ministry is specified. We should have the complete text, you will understand, for the understanding of it. Maybe in addition, some clarification may be reached by asking questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one minute, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this would be of any assistance, Your Honours, I should like to ask the witness to read the item in question, item 11, in total, in the B/C/S, and during the break, we shall, after the break, we shall submit to you the translation of item 11 if that is agreeable, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Maybe not the whole number 11 but the introduction part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it will be a problem to translate the entire point 11 because this is a small piece of text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you can do that, please do that. Thank you very much, Mr. Perovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, would you please read item 11 of the B/C/S version for us, in its entirety? What does it say?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 11, "Within the framework of the Ministry of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in peacetime and in war, illegible," I suppose it should say "should be formed," "brigades of the police according to the following: The 75th Brigade of the police according to establishment number T-590000. Peacetime location and point of mobilisation, Knin. The 79th police Brigade according to establishment number T 590001. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Korenica." Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Read the whole text.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 80th police Brigade according to establish number T 590002. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Vojnic. "The 83rd police Brigade, according to establishment number T-590003. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Petrinja. "The 85th police Brigade, according to establishment number T 590004. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Okucani."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Please scroll up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "87th police Brigade, according to formation" -- sorry, "to establishment number T-590005. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Vukovar." "The 90th police Brigade according to establishment number T-590006. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Beli Manastir. "The 92nd police Brigade according to establishment number T-590007. Peacetime location and mobilisation point, Benkovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: And the last sentence, what was it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Brigades in peacetime and in war are to be subordinated to the administration of special police units of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Perovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, as far as I could grasp, this concerns the need to form eight brigades of special units of police?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Was this order complied in full? Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We complied with it. We started establishing these units, from the moment when JNA forces were withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: How many of these brigades were fully established?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I inspected four full brigades. Four of them were not established in full. And their establishment was not finished because they were to be disbanded at the end of 1992, more precisely under an order of the Chief of the General Staff of the army of Serbian Krajina, I believe that that order was issued on the 28th of November, I think, and they were supposed to cease operations on the 1st of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, what was the task of these special units of police?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main task of those special units of police was to secure the borders of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Why at a certain point this need for them to exist ceased? Why they were disbanded?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were disbanded when the army of Serbian Krajina was established and it was established pursuant to the Serbian -- Republic of Serbian Krajina assembly decision, and the conditions for that establishment of such military were as follows. Up to that point, peacekeeping forces had not complied with their mandate, which was corroborated by the following facts. In June, in the area of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, in the south sector, at Miljevac plateau, we experienced an aggression of the Croatian forces against a UN protected area. 40 Territorial Defence troops were killed, who were deployed in that area and who -- and there were -- their bodies were thrown in the Bacica Mratovske by the Croatian forces and later, with the help of the French contingent of the UN forces, their bodies were retrieved and they were later interred at the Knin cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a second? These units which were disbanded at the end of November 1992 --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: -- what was their formation? What were they part of?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of them entered the complement of the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to what were -- was this done?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to an order, decision, of the assembly of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have Exhibit 576 brought on to the screens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Got it, Mr. Perovic? Or are you having --

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the document marked 576, Exhibit 576. Could you please zoom in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: You don't have it on your screen? Do you have it now?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read to us the heading, the date, and the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republic of Serbian Krajina, General Staff of the Serbian army, state secret number 947-2311 or either /1. Knin, 27th of November 1992, re-establishment of the Territorial Defence and special units of police into the Serbian army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: May we go to page 5 of the original? 6249, the last four digits. In English, that's page 4. Original page 5, English version page 4. Witness, now I would like you to read to us paragraph 2.9, item A and B.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Disband and terminate mobilisation development, A, of the administration of special units of police, men and materiel to be transformed into the establishment of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. B, 75th Brigade of special units of police of Knin, PJM, Knin. Men, equipment and materiel to be transformed into the 75th Motorised Brigade, 1st Light Brigade and the 2nd Infantry Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May we go to page 16 of the original? That's page 13 in the English version. So page 16 B/C/S. In English, that's page 13. May we have you read it, under Roman numeral 2, if you have it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: May we scroll down?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Can you read it out now?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "The following formations are going to be disbanded. All erstwhile establishments of the staffs of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and special units of police of the Republic of Serbian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Please read the last paragraph on this page. That's paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Brigades of PJM, special units of police, will be part of the corps in whose zone of responsibilities they are located in and they are going to be subordinated in all respects to the commanders of the corps, from January -- December 1st 1992, starting from 0001 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, whether this order is the one disbanding the administration of special units of police and the units themselves?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since we are going to broach another subject, and we are nearing the end of the first session, I would propose that we start discussing this other matter at the beginning of the next session, after the break, if you're in agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Perovic. Before we do so, are you able to tell us where in the English translation the last paragraph that the witness read appears? I've been trying to follow through with you. I actually turned the page. I can't find this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 13 in the English translation. The last paragraph on that page. It's supposed to be. It's designated paragraph 4. At least in the B/C/S version, it's designated 4. Under roman numeral 3. So chapter roman numeral 3, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's on page 14, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I thought it was page 13. This is the information that I received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Perovic. Yes, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I also ask something about this document? You said this was the order to disband these units, these special police units. Was it only this or was it at the same time an order to establish something else in place of these units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By this order, Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina was disbanded, and General Staff of the Territorial Defence, zone and municipal staffs of the Territorial Defence, all units of the Territorial Defence, which means detachments and brigades, and lower units, they are -- what else is disbanded completely are the special units of police, and from those two bodies of men, we formed the Serbian army of Krajina and, pursuant to this order, it started operating in December, on the 1st of December, at 0001 hours, one minute after mid-night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: What do you mean by we formed the Serbian Army of Krajina? The order was given by the commander of General Staff of Serbian Army of RSK, Novakovic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I said something wrong when I said, "We." Under "we," I mean the commander of the General Staff of the army of Serbian Krajina. He was the one under constitution and laws of the Republic of Serbian Krajina who had the power to do so because previously by decree of the president of the RSK, he was nominated Chief of the General Staff of the army. I believe that that decree was issued towards the end of November, between 26th and 28th of November 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It would be interesting when between 26th and 28th, as we are reading, an order of 27th of November of the commander of the General Staff of Serbian army of the RSK. An order which is forming the Serbian army of the RSK. You understand what I'm sort of missing? What's the missing link?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Previously, a presidential decree, General Novakovic was nominated as commander and promoted to the rank of general before this order was issued. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is what I needed for understanding it. Thank you very much. I have got what I wanted, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that time is ripe for a break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Perovic. We will take a short break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Perovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, I only have one more question related to the topic that we discussed at the previous session. Do [as interpreted] the representatives of the United Nations have any objections to the actions and functions -- functioning of the special police units, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Perovic, did you say do or did they?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Did, said the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The translation said"do." Okay. So it's "did." Okay, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Past perfect tense. I as the head of the administration of the special police units upon the arrival of the peace forces, I established contact with representatives and commanders of the contingence of the peace forces, the representatives of the police, and the representative for civilian affairs, at which time I mostly liaised, had contacts with Mr. Kirudja. At that time, with their protocol, which they had in written form, we -- using that protocol, we elaborated our own instructions for the work of special police units on the ground, elaborating all procedures in detail according to their proposal and the assistance they gave us in elaborating that document. These representatives never had any objections on the ground. There perhaps might have been a petty incident here or there, but the reason for that was because those units were on the line or actually in the buffer zone, and we were carrying out that task, and they were deployed at certain points, while most of their forces were in cities, in facilities which were dedicated to their -- to them for their use by the government of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina. However, we were surprised at a report which mentioned the existence, just the existence, of the special police units. After that report, we established contact with Mr. Kirudja, the then-minister, Mr. Martic, was with me on that occasion, and we agreed that we should reduce the strength in two stages, and that the deadline for the reduction of the strength of the police units should be sometime October 1992. However, in that period, as I said, the Miljevacki plateau occurred, and in the area or Sector North, in Slunj, in the area of Slunj, from the territory of Croatia, sometime in August, via the territory of Slunj, to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina or more precisely the Cazin Krajina for the 5th Corps of the B and H army was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you, Mr. Djukic, you have already answered my question which was, did the representatives of the United Nations have any objections to the actions and functioning of the special police units?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were only commended by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In further proceeding I shall return to something that we have already broached as a subject at previous sessions. Mr. Djukic, you personally took part in the unblocking of the road through the village of Kijevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What kind of a village was this? And when I say "this," what village was I referring to the ethnicity of its residents [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a Croatian, Croat-populated village. The Croats -- the number of residents was between 1.000 and 1.500.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To what municipality did it belong?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It belonged to the municipality of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: During yesterday's examination, you mentioned that the new Croatian government had set up a police station in this village. What was the reason for the establishment of a police station in a place where it had not existed before?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: O, it is true that I did say a police station had been set up in the village of Kijevo. In the first batch, 50 MUP members were sent to the police station, headed by Ivica Bucic, an inspector of the police of the MUP of Croatia, and there never had existed a police station there before. It was set up in order to, together with able-bodied residents of the village, form a volunteer -- a detachment of volunteers and for it as a para police station to contribute to the forming of -- the further forming of the army of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these forces stationed at Kijevo reinforced at any point and if you remember that that was the case, when was that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the situation which obtained there, and the constant threats and the constant incidents, of which there had been a number, that station was reinforced by forces from Split, the Split police station. Reinforcements were brought from there, and by mid-August it had about 150 members of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia. In addition, the neighbouring village of Mauvica [phoen] also had between 150 and 200 members of the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia as well. In the village they managed to arm all able-bodied men capable of combat, forming a detachment of volunteers or a unit of volunteers for national defence which according to our figures had about 200 plus members so that this contingent reinforced those forces in the village proper, namely that meant that the number of army was -- corresponded to the number of residents, speaking in pejorative terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude -- what was the attitude of the JNA to the forces in Kijevo?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attitude they had was as ordered by the leadership. When the JNA was proclaimed hostile, that police station also adopted the same position. We had some problems there. They blocked the passage of JNA units through the village so that we were unable at certain moments to ensure the supply of the delivery of food, water to members of the unit, of units which were in the buffer zones, which we had behind that village, namely in the direction of Knin and Sinj where we had two buffer zones so that we were even forced to have helicopter drops to supply those buffer zones. We had a case of appendicitis of one of our soldiers and we took him in an ambulance but we were not allowed to pass and this irritated no end the people, the villagers, as well as the army, the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the position of the Serb population, the -- towards such a situation in Kijevo? What did the Serbs from the neighbouring villages and Kijevo demand?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The Serbs from Knin not from Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in summer, parts Donji and Gornji Civljani, other neighbouring villages, most of the population of these villages worked in Knin, were employed in Knin's factories. There were several factories there, for instance the Tvik, the bolt and screws factory, and that there was a knitted goods factory, printing plant, and so on and so forth. And they were prohibited from passing, from going there, so that they used some paths, goat paths, across the Dinara mountain in order to get to work. And another thing, there were different incidents also. One of those which actually prompted the population in Knin to assemble was the prohibition for the mortal remains of one person who had been killed in the police station in Sibenik, he was -- his name was Dusan Vranjis who was taken off the bus in Zupanja, this is a place between Serbia and Croatia up north, and the transfer to the Rijeka prison, and then from Rijeka to Sibenik, and then in Sibenik he was killed. As they wouldn't let his relatives pass through that village and for him to be buried in Civljani, the people assembled at the -- Knin's railway station and in front of the command of the 9th corps, the people demanded to be distributed weapons and at that time, the leader of the Serbs, of the Serbian democratic party, Dr. Jovan Raskovic, said, and I quote, "I will not lead you into war. I will lead you to peace." And he asked the people to disassemble and not to ask the army for arms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, Mr. Perovic, I'm sorry, I just need clarification here. It may be a question of interpretation. You said in this answer there was a prohibition of the passing of the mortal remains, and then while talking about those mortal remains, you said he was taken to some other place and killed. Now, this was already a dead person. How do we kill a dead person?

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness will explain this the best. Actually he perhaps confused the chronology a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: This person, Dusan Vranjis had first -- was he arrested in Zupanja.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken off the bus and arrested in Zupanja, which is a place, as I said, just after the border of Serbia and Croatia, up north, on the highway. He was then transferred to the Rijeka prison. He was killed in the police prison in Sibenik after that. His mortal remains were supposed to be transported from Sibenik via Drnis, Knin, and through Kijevo to -- of course, in a funeral hearse, to the village of will have where they were to be buried at the local cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is a full answer, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Djukic, after all these incidents which evidently were numerous, what specifically brought about the de-blockade, i.e., the opening of the road through Kijevo? When did this exactly happen and what was it preceded immediately by?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general position of the Croatian leadership was to provoke incidents at that time. And I corroborate this by the fact that the president of Croatia, Mr. Franjo Tudjman, in an official address, said, "The war wouldn't have happened had we not wanted it." And this has been repeated here time and again. Namely, in the area of Dalmatia the idea was to create a situation rife with incidents, in order to mobilise to the maximum the Croatian population in a struggle against the then Yugoslav People's Army and normally in expelling the Serbian people from those areas. On the 25th of August 1991, para formations, para units of Croatia, in other words the detachments of volunteers and the MUP of Vrlika reinforced with forces from Sinj attacked the buffer zone which I talked about which was between Gornji Civljani and went through the village of Lelas and Donji Civljani and the -- Kosare and Cetina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Witness, when you say they attacked the buffer zone I understand you to be saying they attacked the Yugoslav People's Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They attacked the Yugoslav People's Army. In that attack, [inaudible] repelled a unit commanded by platoon commander Ostoja Goracic [phoen]. That was a mechanised unit with three APCs. The Croatian forces managed to enter Gornjici, the hamlet of Dragici, and in the morning sometime in the morning, having entered, they killed two villagers, Cvita Matcevic and Djordje Matcevic, who were not spouses, and the JNA unit was repelled into the depth, some two and a half kilometres. On the same day, the forces, these reinforced forces from Kijevo --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt the witness. I thought he had finished his answer. I meant to ask a clarification after the witness had finished his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may finish your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On that same day, from the territory of the village of Kijevo, MUP forces carried out an attack on the other two buffer zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. To make it short, so these attacks on the buffer zones were the direct cause for intervention, i.e., action, related to the village of Kijevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague had a question, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I also now have an objection to that last question which was incredibly leading. But I wasn't able to jump up in time. But the clarification I was seeking, Your Honour, actually to do with a couple of minutes ago and I'm sorry for being tardy but I was checking the transcript. I just wondered if because it was missed in the transcript, if the village where this person Dusan Vranjis was supposed to be buried in, if that -- if the name of that village could just be repeated because I don't have it in the transcript and I'm interested to hear it, if that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you hear the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, the name of the village is Cetina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, need I respond to my learned colleague's objection? I understand that he objected to my question as being leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Perovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, briefly, I am unable to perceive the leading nature of my question. I just wanted to shorten the answer of the witness because my question was what caused the specific action in Kijevo because he had already listed the attacks on the buffer zone. I summarised them in my question and asked him whether he considered those attacks on the buffer zones the concrete cause for the attack on Kijevo, so I failed to perceive what is leading on my part in that connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think the witness had answered the question and it's either leading or it's asked and answered, and there is no need to ask it again. So I don't think there was any need for it and in the form that it was put to the witness, it's plainly leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was leading, yes, it is ruled that the question is leading. Thank you. Mr. Perovic, it's answered. There is no need to do anything about it. Just carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: So, under whose orders was this intervention in the village of Kijevo performed?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intervention in the village of Kijevo was done on the -- under the orders of the commander of the 9th Corps, General Spiro Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did it take? How long did it last to de-blockade the road through Kijevo?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That operation lasted only a couple of hours. It was finished at 1200 hours on the 25th. Only one remark concerning that. I ordered the units not to take a path through Kijevo but to execute a pincer movement to reach the main point of resistance, the cemetery and the church, to disarm the parapolice and paramilitary troops of Croatia. I can tell you that this action was brilliantly planned and executed. None of the members of the JNA were either wounded or killed, and as far as I can -- I know, there were no casualties, nobody was killed or wounded, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: So there were no people killed, nor wounded. Were there any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that action, units under my command captured 60 members of the MUP in the village of Kijevo. I continued this action to reinstate the buffer zone near Vrlika in the Gornji Civljani, the hamlet of Dragici as I mentioned, a couple of hours after that. This was done, and in that area, my troops captured an additional 12 members of the MUP and volunteer detachments of Croatia, and over all 72 of them were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What happened to them?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police unit took over. We secured bus transportation. We disarmed them and we sent it to the military investigation prison of the 9th Corps in the north barracks in Knin, and they were exchanged in a couple of days' time, according to the all-for-all principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At a previous session, we discussed Drnis, lifted the blockade of military facilities within that municipality. Briefly, since you took part in that operation, could you tell us what happened then at Drnis and it's surroundings and what facilities, which facilities were de-blockaded previously having been blockaded?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that it's the third time that the Zitnic depot was blockaded beyond Drnis next to the road between Drnis and Sibenik, and another facility was the 55th navy technical rocket base of Trbounje, in the village of Trbounje, since it's eponymous, and the wider area we call the Miljevac plateau. In a, when the Croatian president, Mr. Franjo Tudjman, ordered general attack against all JNA units on the 15th of September 1991, all units of the military naval district came under attack in Split, in Sibenik, in Zadar, in Sinj, and the two facilities within the area of responsibility of the 9th Corps. My task was to lift the blockade of the Zitnic depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: How long did this action take?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It started at 1600 hours, during the night I transported infantry through the -- and over the Mosez mountain, under the orders of the command to avoid transportation through Drnis, and by morning hours, I managed to connect with the units defending the Zitnic depot. This was accomplished, and the other side, during the night, organised the withdrawal of the population on a side road through the village of Knezovi, Noskalik [phoen] towards Skradin, and further to Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Just a second. I believe that you failed to mention the date. You said the hour but not the date.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date was the 16th of September, at 1600 hours. A day later we started one day later because of the very difficult situation both in Sibenik and these facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What was the outcome?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The outcome was that the next day, at 1300 hours, I went through Drnis without any significant resistance, and reached the line connecting Zitnic, the road, I mean, and the forces with whom I had coordinated actions but commanded by the commander of the technical group 2, continued to lift the blockade of the 55th Motorised Brigade facilities. This task was accomplished without a single wounded or killed troop, and I don't have information about casualties on -- of the other side. I believe that there were no casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, you took part in the lifting of the blockade of the Sibenik barracks. You commanded that action?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. A part of that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: A part of that action. When did the blockade of the Sibenik barracks start, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blockade of the Sibenik barracks began as early as the 5th of May, after President Tudjman's speech as Trogir. Then MUP and volunteer detachments, organised a wider blockade of the barracks. They cut off water supply, power supply, telephone lines to the command and the barracks. In and around Sibenik there were several facilities, commander of the military section, the JNA home, then marine brigade, the command of the sector, the docking port, the Kumane [phoen] barracks and the general -- and this blockade lasted throughout the summer. And the general attack started on the 15th of September 1991. And after having lifted the blockade at Drnis, the command of the corps took action to lift the blockade of the barracks at Sibenik, to save the members of the JNA, their families, and the property of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Who issued the order for the lifting of the blockades?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was issued by the commander of the 9th Corps, General -- Lieutenant General Vlado Vukovic, Vladimir Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: When did you start implementing this order?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Sibenik we started implementing this order on the 21st of September. We reached the village of Bilice on the outskirts of Sibenik by the night, and other forces from the corps command acted on the right side of the river Krka on the direction between Kistanje, the village of Popovici and the Sibenik bridge. This is the bridge of the Dalmatian coast trunk line which connects to Zadar, Sibenik, and Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: Your action of the 21st of September, was it preceded by anything?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was preceded by very difficult situation obtaining in Sibenik. I can explain that. We received reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this: When did Second Lieutenant General Vukovic issue this order to lift the blockade of Sibenik?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of September, and after the lifting of the blockade of Drnis facilities, this was a continuation of the same order and the same task with a view of lifting the blockade of -- against JNA facilities in Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: When did this action begin?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, on the 16th. As I said. But when -- with regard to Sibenik it started on the 21st, and when it came to Sinj, it started on the 16th and the forces advancing towards Sinj connected with other units on the 21st or 22nd of September, 22nd or 23rd, correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What was the outcome of the action to lift the blockade of Sibenik?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we asked -- when we reached the village of Glavica towards the outskirts of Sibenik, the Croatian leadership insisted that we conclude a cease-fire agreement. There was talk between the federal secretary of National Defence, General Kadijevic, and personally he took -- talked to President Tudjman. I believe that these transcripts have been discussed here. I can only say that the federal secretary wanted the barracks to be de-blockaded so that forces could be withdrawn, and that we do not wage war. But the final cease-fire was concluded in the village of Zitnic on the 25th of September. General Vukovic signed the cease-fire agreement on behalf of the JNA and on behalf of the then Croatian government, who signed the agreement, was the then-maritime minister, Mr. Davorin Rudolf. I know that because I was there making arrangements. I believe that this was the 14th cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: What was arranged and agreed upon during that cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was agreed that all units of the JNA, all equipment and materiel, the family members of JNA members, to be withdrawn without impediment from Sibenik, Split, but this cease-fire agreement did not encompass the withdrawal of JNA members, their families, from the Zadar garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. PEROVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take to withdraw JNA troops, their family members, from Sibenik and Sinj?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
